name: Riyadh
operatingHours: Riyadh Metro (six driverless lines, fully open since January 2025) runs ~6:00 AM–~midnight daily, with later starts on Friday mornings and extended hours during major events; trains every ~4–8 min at peaks. Each train has a First Class car and a family section. RCRC Riyadh Bus routes cover the rest of the city.
fareInfo: One ticket covers metro and bus: 2 hours SAR 4, 3 days SAR 20, 7 days SAR 40, 30 days SAR 140 (First Class SAR 10 / 50 / 100 / 350). Tap a contactless bank card or phone at the gates, or buy via the Darb app or station machines; 50% off for students, seniors and people with disabilities.

sights.name: Kingdom Centre Sky Bridge
sights.note: A 300 m-high steel walkway spanning the opening at the top of Riyadh's bottle-opener-shaped Kingdom Tower, reached by two fast lifts, with sweeping views over Olaya.

sights.name: National Museum
sights.note: A modern museum in the King Abdulaziz Historical Center tracing Arabia from prehistory and the early Islamic era to the unification of the kingdom, with well-designed galleries in English and Arabic.

sights.name: Al Masmak Fortress
sights.note: A mud-brick fort with corner watchtowers in old Deera, stormed by Ibn Saud in 1902 in the raid that began the Saudi state; currently listed as temporarily closed.
sights.hours: Temporarily closed (Oct 2026); view the exterior from Deera's squares

sights.name: Al Rajhi Grand Mosque
sights.note: One of Riyadh's largest mosques, in the eastern Al Jazirah district, built in a restrained traditional Najdi style with tall minarets and a vast courtyard.
sights.hours: Open for the five daily prayers; visitors should dress modestly and avoid prayer times

sights.name: Al Faisaliah Centre
sights.note: Riyadh's first skyscraper, a tapering tower crowned by a golden glass globe that holds a viewing deck and restaurant.

sights.name: King Abdullah Park
sights.note: A large family park in Al Malaz with lawns, a lake and an evening musical fountain show.
sights.hours: ~4:00 PM–midnight daily; fountain shows in the evening

sights.name: Tahlia Street
sights.note: Prince Mohammed bin Abdulaziz Road, Riyadh's café and restaurant strip between King Fahd Road and Olaya, at its liveliest late at night.

sights.name: King Khalid Grand Mosque
sights.note: An elegant white mosque in Umm Al Hamam with a broad dome and slim minarets, especially striking when lit after sunset.
sights.hours: Open for the five daily prayers; dress modestly

sights.name: Salam Park
sights.note: A big green park just south of Deera with a lake, palm groves and walking paths, popular for evening picnics.

sights.name: Murabba Palace
sights.note: King Abdulaziz's 1930s mud-brick palace in the King Abdulaziz Historical Center, with restored courtyards, royal rooms and his vintage cars nearby.

sights.name: Imam Turki bin Abdullah Grand Mosque
sights.note: Riyadh's central Friday mosque on Deera's Justice Square, rebuilt in the 1990s in Najdi style with square minarets and connected to the Qasr Al Hukm palace by a bridge.
sights.hours: Open for the five daily prayers; dress modestly

sights.name: At-Turaif District (Diriyah)
sights.note: The restored mud-brick citadel of the first Saudi state on the edge of Wadi Hanifa, a UNESCO site with palaces, museums and evening light shows.
sights.hours: ~5:00 PM–midnight daily (ticketed; hours vary by season)

sights.name: Bujairi Terrace
sights.note: A palm-shaded dining terrace across the wadi from At-Turaif, with Najdi architecture, restaurants and views of the floodlit ruins.

sights.name: Souq Al Zal
sights.note: Riyadh's oldest market in Deera, with lanes of carpets, incense, daggers, antiques and an informal evening auction.

railStations.name: Riyadh Railway Station
railStations.note: SAR's station in the Sinaiyah/Malaz district for trains east to Hofuf and Dammam (~4 h); the Railway stop on Metro Line 3 (Orange) is alongside, on the subway map.
railStations.hours: Trains by timetable, several a day.

railStations.name: Riyadh North Railway Station
railStations.note: SAR's north-line terminus on Al Thumamah Road for trains to Al Qassim, Ha'il and Al Jouf; isolated near the airport and not on the metro, so plan a taxi or app ride.
railStations.hours: Trains by timetable, a few a day.

airports.name: King Khalid International Airport
airports.transitNote: Metro Line 4 (Yellow, on the subway map) runs from stations at Terminals 1–2, 3–4 and 5 to KAFD in ~30–35 min (SAR 4), with changes to the Blue, Red and Purple lines for Olaya and the centre. Taxis and app cabs take ~30–45 min to Olaya.
airports.hours: Metro ~6:00 AM–~midnight. Late arrivals: taxi or app cab.
